author: high
claim: Direct inverse construction proves the target. Metadata: statement = If Q is a real orthogonal n-by-n matrix with no nonzero fixed vector and u is a unit vector, then for H=I-2uu^{\mathsf T}, the vector w=(I-Q)^{-1}u is nonzero and satisfies HQw=w; justification_type = calculation; confidence = 1.0; is_fragile = false; fragility_reason = ""; suggested_followup = none; scope = global.
evidence: The hypothesis Qv=v only for v=0 gives ker(I-Q)={0}, hence the square map I-Q is invertible. Define w=(I-Q)^{-1}u. Then (I-Q)w=u, so Qw=w-u. Since Q is orthogonal, ||w||^2=||Qw||^2=||w-u||^2=||w||^2-2u^{\mathsf T}w+||u||^2. As ||u||^2=1, this gives u^{\mathsf T}w=1/2. Therefore u^{\mathsf T}Qw=u^{\mathsf T}(w-u)=-1/2, and HQw=Qw-2u(u^{\mathsf T}Qw)=w-u+u=w. Finally w cannot be zero because (I-Q)w=u and u is nonzero.

glossary.n: the positive integer dimension of the real vector space
glossary.Q: the given real n-by-n orthogonal matrix
